sections.context: SPEC.md (trellis repo root) is the locked design record for trellis: a mostly-deterministic, partly-agentic audit tool that scores a fleet of repos against a versioned 90-criterion / 9-category agent-readiness rubric (44 repo-scope + 46 app-scope criteria; 70 deterministic, 20 agent-investigated), maps pass rate to maturity Level 1-5 with a coverage-aware clamp, detects canonical-config drift (L1) against a bundled standards/ set, and persists every run in central SQLite for drift attribution over time. The LLM layer is bounded: 4 fixed investigation areas run via Pi in RPC mode (read-only tools + a submit_findings extension tool), returning zod-validated facts that a deterministic grader converts to pass/fail — same facts, same grade; findings are cached per (repo, commit, area). trellis is a greenfield os-eco sub-repo and must itself meet the os-eco repo standards it audits for (eat-its-own-dogfood, SPEC §13: score L4+ against itself). Those standards, surveyed from warren (reference L5 implementation), seeds/canopy (published CLIs), and templates/l5-toolkit (canonical portable artifacts), are: Bun + TypeScript strict (noUncheckedIndexedAccess, no any) + Biome --error-on-warnings + zod + commander + pino + bun:sqlite; kebab-case filenames, tab indent / 100-col, .ts import extensions, <name>.test.ts beside the unit, golden fixtures under __golden__/; standard root files (README, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, CHANGELOG keep-a-changelog, CODEOWNERS, CONTRIBUTING, SECURITY, LICENSE MIT, RUNBOOK); .claude/commands/release.md (patch-default bump, package.json + src VERSION sync, CHANGELOG roll) plus pr-reviews/issue-reviews/prioritize; .github governance (dependabot with cooldown, ISSUE_TEMPLATEs, PR template, labels.yml + sync-labels.yml, ci.yml running check:all verbatim, version-gated publish.yml to npm with provenance, auto-merge.yml); the L5 toolkit ratchet scripts + budgets + validate-agents-md + reporters + pre-commit hook wired into a check:all aggregator; .seeds/ + .mulch/ instances; npm package @os-eco/trellis-cli with bin trellis.
sections.approach: Build in the SPEC §14 milestone order, but put the os-eco standards scaffold FIRST (steps 1-4) so every subsequent step lands on a repo whose gates (lint/typecheck/test/check:all/CI) are already enforcing the conventions — the tool that audits standards is built under those standards from commit one. Then follow the data-flow seam: rubric data + schema (the WHAT, steps 5-7), pure scoring engine (8), deterministic detector infrastructure and the TypeScript adapter (9-12), a first end-to-end det-only audit of warren with terminal/JSON/MD renderers (13), then the remaining language adapters (14-15), the SQLite store (16), the investigation layer built goldens-first so CI never makes model calls (17-20), canonical-standards drift (21-22), fleet + history reporting (23-24), os-eco-native detectors (25), the typed SDK + CI-usable exit-code contract (26), the dogfood gate (27), and the v0.1.0 release (28). Forward-blocking edges encode the real dependency graph rather than strict linearity, so independent tracks (e.g. Swift/Python adapters, canonical standards extraction, investigation schemas) can be picked up in parallel by separate agents as their inputs clear. Every step is sized for a single agent run: one coherent module with its tests, landing on main with the full gate suite green. The api>cli>sdk discipline (SPEC §13.1) is enforced structurally from step 7 onward: all behavior in surface-agnostic core modules, CLI and SDK as thin pass-throughs, so the surfaces cannot drift.

alternatives.name: Build the audit engine first and retrofit the os-eco standards scaffold (ratchets, CI, governance) at the end
alternatives.rejected_because: trellis's own credibility rests on dogfooding (SPEC §13: it should score L4+ against itself). Retrofitting ratchets onto a finished codebase means baselining budgets against accumulated debt; scaffolding first means every commit lands under the gates, and the dogfood step (27) verifies rather than remediates.

alternatives.name: Score everything with an LLM end-to-end instead of the deterministic-core + bounded-investigation split
alternatives.rejected_because: Violates the SPEC's determinism mandate (identical repo → identical output). 70 of 90 criteria are file/config/command checks that need no model; the 20 fuzzy criteria return facts (not verdicts) graded deterministically, keeping re-runs reproducible and CI offline.

alternatives.name: TypeScript-only MVP, defer Swift and Python adapters
alternatives.rejected_because: SPEC §2 explicitly puts all three languages in MVP goals — the operator's fleet includes a Swift project and soon a Python project, and the rubric's tool-agnostic WHAT / per-language HOW seam is only proven by a second and third adapter.

alternatives.name: Live Pi calls in the investigation test suite
alternatives.rejected_because: SPEC §9.7 mandates golden fixtures: capture one real RPC session per area, canonicalize volatile fields, freeze; parser → zod → grader run entirely offline and CI never makes model calls. Live calls are gated behind TRELLIS_UPDATE_PI_GOLDEN=1 plus an explicit flag.

alternatives.name: Per-repo committed scorecards instead of central SQLite history
alternatives.rejected_because: SPEC §2 non-goal: state is central (one SQLite DB keyed by targets.yaml ids), so audited repos are never written to (read-only mandate) and fleet drift queries stay cheap.

alternatives.name: Strictly linear plan (each step blocks only its successor)
alternatives.rejected_because: Several tracks are genuinely independent — language adapters, canonical standards extraction, investigation schemas vs Pi transport — and serializing them wastes parallel agent capacity. Forward-blocking edges encode the actual dependency graph; sd ready surfaces whatever is truly unblocked.

alternatives.name: Include L3 auto-fix (Warren fan-out), weighted scoring, or the web dashboard in this plan
alternatives.rejected_because: All explicitly deferred in SPEC §15. gate/weight fields are authored but reserved; auto-fix builds only after the read-only signal is trusted; the dashboard is a later surface over the same core.

steps.title: Scaffold the repo: Bun + TS-strict skeleton, os-eco baseline configs, package.json (@os-eco/trellis-cli, bin trellis), src/ tree per SPEC §4

Author governance & agent docs: README, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, CHANGELOG, CODEOWNERS, CONTRIBUTING, SECURITY, RUNBOOK, docs/architecture.mmd, .claude/commands (release, pr-reviews, issue-reviews, prioritize), .mulch init
Port the L5 quality toolkit: ratchet scripts + baselined budgets, validate-agents-md, reporters, pre-commit hook, check:* family wired into a green check:all

Add .github governance + workflows: dependabot (cooldown), ISSUE_TEMPLATEs, PR template, labels.yml, ci.yml (check:all parity), sync-labels.yml, publish.yml (version-gated npm + provenance), auto-merge.yml
Rubric schema + loader: zod schemas for criterion/category records, RUBRIC_VERSION + comparability policy, load-time invariants (SPEC §6.1)
Author the rubric data: categories.yaml (9), repo-scope.yaml (44), app-scope.yaml (46) — the full §5 catalog with levels, gates, skippable flags, discoveryVia/investigation tags
CLI skeleton (thin commander entrypoints over the domain core, SPEC §13.1) + first end-to-end command: trellis rubric [--validate]
Scoring engine: per-criterion score, pass rate, coverage clamp, naKind handling, 20-pt bands, repo/app aggregation — pure functions unit-tested against §3.4 worked examples
Detector infrastructure: DetectionContext + DetectorResult contract (SPEC §8.1), criterion→detector registry, not-applicable vs no-detector discipline
App discovery (SPEC §8.2): find independently-deployable directories as apps; 0 found → repo root is 1 app; app map recorded in the report

Common language-agnostic detectors: gitignore, env template, CI/workflow presence, CODEOWNERS, branch protection via VCS CLI, dependabot, issue/PR templates, release automation, and the rest of detectors/common/
TypeScript adapter detectors: Biome, tsc strict flags, knip, jscpd, bun test, coverage ratchets, import cycles, and the TS-specific Locality & Contracts checks
Report renderers (terminal/JSON/MD, §6.3 shape) + trellis audit <repo-path> det-only end-to-end against warren — agent criteria resolve no-detector for now
Swift adapter detectors: SwiftLint, swift build/test, swift-format, periphery, coverage — with honest not-applicable mapping for concepts Swift lacks
Python adapter detectors: ruff, mypy --strict, pytest, coverage.py, vulture, deptry, grimp/pydeps — with honest not-applicable mapping
SQLite store (bun:sqlite): schema.sql + migrations for runs / criterion_results / investigation_cache (SPEC §6.4), audit persistence wired in
Investigation layer core: the 4 fixed areas (areas.ts), zod findings schemas per area (findings.ts), and the pure deterministic grader (facts → pass/fail/N-A, SPEC §7)

Pi RPC provider (SPEC §9): argv builder, findings-extension.ts (submit_findings tool), JSONL event loop, env passthrough, corrective-prompt retries, heartbeat watchdog, version probe + graceful no-detector degradation

Golden fixtures + offline test harness (SPEC §9.7): captured + canonicalized Pi RPC sessions per area under __golden__/, parser → zod → grader exercised fully offline, TRELLIS_UPDATE_PI_GOLDEN regeneration gate
Wire investigation into audit: investigate() core entrypoint, investigation_cache keyed (repo, commit_sha, area), --no-cache flag, agent criteria flow into the scorecard
Canonical standards set: src/standards/canonical/ files extracted from the l5-toolkit/warren conventions + manifest.yaml with per-file semver, hashes, and matcher kinds (SPEC §10)

Drift engine: drift.ts matchers (exact/json-subset/yaml-subset/text/template), allowed-deltas, per-file states (match/allowed-delta/drift/missing/extra), trellis drift + trellis standards commands, report.drift
Fleet: targets.yaml loader (defaults, per-target canonical overrides + allowedDeltas, skip, osecoDetectors, languages) + trellis fleet multi-repo orchestration
History reporting: trellis report dashboard from SQLite (--repo/--since/--json/--md) + changes-since-last-run deltas with rubric-version attribution (SPEC §11)
os-eco-native detectors (SPEC §8.4): seeds/mulch/canopy/plot/skills/check:all/ratchet evidence mapped onto existing criteria, osecoDetectors per-target toggle
Typed SDK (src/client/) mirroring core types + CLI exit-code contract (--fail-on level|gate|drift|none) so trellis is CI-usable per repo (SPEC §12, §13.1)
Dogfood gate: trellis audits itself (must band L4+) and the warren-stack fleet end-to-end; iterate detector bindings on what actually mattered
Release v0.1.0: CHANGELOG roll, version sync (package.json + src VERSION), publish @os-eco/trellis-cli via the version-gated workflow

risks: Pi RPC wire format is version-sensitive (burrow pins v0.74.0): mitigate by documenting a supported Pi version, probing via pi --version at startup, and degrading every agent criterion to no-detector instead of crashing (SPEC §9.6).

Authoring 90 rubric criteria by hand is error-prone: mitigated by zod load-time invariants (investigation iff agent, exactly one gate per category, scope/file match, weight > 0) and trellis rubric --validate as the milestone-1 acceptance gate.
Clean-room discipline: the rubric is a de-branded reimplementation of the private v0.2.0 source — no verbatim code or data may be copied from notes/PRIVATE-rubric (SPEC Appendix A).
Detector tool availability varies per machine: the configured-for-but-unavailable case must resolve to no-detector (counted against coverage), never a false pass or a crash.
LLM nondeterminism leaking into scores: contained by the (repo, commit, area) findings cache — nondeterminism is a one-time cost per commit, not a per-run coin flip.
Scope creep into deferred features (Warren fan-out auto-fix, weighted scoring, web dashboard, the 10th category): all live in SPEC §15 and are out of plan.
Read-only mandate: an audit must never mutate the target repo — Pi runs with a read-only tool allowlist and no detector shells out to anything that writes.
acceptance: trellis rubric --validate passes: 9 categories, 44 repo-scope + 46 app-scope criteria, exactly 9 gates, all schema invariants green.
trellis audit <warren-path> runs end-to-end deterministically (det-only and with cached/golden investigation findings) and emits terminal, JSON, and markdown scorecards matching the §6.3 shape.
The investigation test suite runs entirely offline against golden fixtures; CI makes zero model calls; a missing/incompatible Pi degrades agent criteria to no-detector without crashing.
trellis drift reports match/allowed-delta/drift/missing/extra per canonical file, honoring targets.yaml allowedDeltas.
trellis fleet audits every target in targets.yaml and persists runs/criterion_results to central SQLite; trellis report renders history with changes-since-last-run and rubric-version attribution.
Identical repo at identical commit → byte-identical scorecard (determinism mandate).

The repo itself carries the full os-eco standard: all root files, .claude/commands/release.md, .github governance + ci/publish/sync-labels workflows, ratchets + check:all green locally and in CI (parity).
Dogfood: trellis scores L4+ against itself at the dogfood gate.
bun test, bun run lint, bun run typecheck, and bun run check:all all exit 0 on main at every step's landing commit.
v0.1.0 of @os-eco/trellis-cli is ready to publish via the version-gated workflow with package.json and src VERSION in sync.

sections.context: trellis already has the canonical terse check scripts plus lint and typecheck, but its check:all is an 8-gate && chain in a non-canonical order (check:coverage runs FIRST, lint/typecheck second) with no quiet runner, no `verify` alias, and no check:ci-parity. Conforming to docs/check-all-standard.md (os-eco-9048) means adopting the byte-identical runner (os-eco-5db7), fixing gate order, and adding the missing gates. Depends on root tracker pl-760e steps 1-2.
sections.approach: Swap the && chain for the canonical quiet runner with a GATES manifest in the standard's order (cheap static gates first, check:coverage second-to-last, check:ci-parity last), then add the generalized ci-parity gate and the verify alias. trellis has no UI bundle or OpenAPI surface, so conditional gates are out of scope; only the core gate set applies.

steps.title: Add the canonical scripts/check-all.ts quiet runner copied byte-identical from templates/l5-toolkit/scripts/check-all.ts, with trellis's exported GATES manifest reordered into the standard's order: lint, typecheck, check:agents, check:dups, check:deps, check:size, check:debt, check:coverage, check:ci-parity (last) -- moving check:coverage out of the leading position it currently holds. Replace package.json check:all with `bun scripts/check-all.ts`, add `verify`: `bun run check:all`, and add scripts/check-all.test.ts. Confirm the quiet-output contract.

Add scripts/check-ci-parity.ts (with test) copied from templates/l5-toolkit/scripts, importing the GATES array from check-all.ts; add the check:ci-parity script as the final gate in the manifest. Reconcile any residual non-canonical gate name. Verify check:ci-parity passes against .github/workflows/ci.yml.

Wire .github/workflows/ci.yml to invoke the canonical gates (or `bun run check:all`) so the local manifest matches CI. Run `bun run check:all` and `bun run verify` green end-to-end with the quiet-output contract and a passing check:ci-parity.

acceptance: check:all is `bun scripts/check-all.ts` with the byte-identical runner and a GATES manifest in the standard's canonical order; verify aliases check:all.
scripts/check-ci-parity.ts imports GATES and passes against .github/workflows/ci.yml.
`bun run check:all` runs green with the quiet-output contract.
